items.title: Foundation lifecycle and synchronization scope
items.statement: LSPS-062 requires client integration, an in-memory registry, configuration loading, per-server process lifecycle over stdio, initialization and shutdown, and document synchronization including debounce, versions, close, save, and supported incremental sync.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The implementation phase guide requires a foundation with client crate integration, in-memory registry, config loading, spawn/lifecycle, stdio transport, initialize handshake, shutdown/exit, and document sync with debounce, versioning, didClose, didSave, and incremental sync when supported.

items.title: Server lifecycle failure and recovery are unspecified
items.statement: The foundation requires spawn and lifecycle behavior but does not define observable behavior for spawn failure, unexpected process exit, restart policy, retry limits, backoff, or restoration of synchronized documents.
items.impact: Implementations can diverge on whether a failed language server remains offline, restarts indefinitely, or loses document state.
items.builder_discretion: Choose failure states, restart eligibility, retry/backoff policy, and resynchronization behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The implementation phase guide requires a foundation with client crate integration, in-memory registry, config loading, spawn/lifecycle, stdio transport, initialize handshake, shutdown/exit, and document sync with debounce, versioning, didClose, didSave, and incremental sync when supported.

items.title: Diagnostics UI acceptance behavior
items.statement: Diagnostics are stored per URI and exposed to the UI; acceptance requires errors and warnings in Problems, gutter markers, and click-through to the diagnostic line.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Diagnostics implementation subscribes to publishDiagnostics, stores diagnostics per URI, exposes them to the UI, and accepts completion when Problems shows errors and warnings, gutter markers render, and clicking opens the file at the diagnostic line.

items.title: Diagnostic freshness and clearing rules are absent
items.statement: Per-URI storage is required, but the unit does not specify version ordering, rejection of stale diagnostics, replacement versus accumulation, empty-publication clearing, or cleanup after document close and server exit.
items.impact: Problems and gutter state can retain obsolete diagnostics or display results for an older document version.
items.builder_discretion: Define diagnostic store update, staleness, clearing, and lifecycle semantics.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Diagnostics implementation subscribes to publishDiagnostics, stores diagnostics per URI, exposes them to the UI, and accepts completion when Problems shows errors and warnings, gutter markers render, and clicking opens the file at the diagnostic line.

items.title: LSP-backed editor navigation with stale-result rejection
items.statement: Hover, completion, symbols, definition, references, breadcrumbs, and go-to-symbol use LSP when available, and stale hover, completion, or navigation responses must be discarded.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Hover, completion, documentSymbol, definition, references, breadcrumbs, and go-to-symbol features use LSP when available, enforce timeout/cancel/stale handling, and accept completion when hover, completion, breadcrumbs, symbol, and definition navigation work correctly.
- Stale hover/completion/navigation responses must be discarded.

items.title: Timeout and cancellation transitions lack a contract
items.statement: Timeout, cancellation, and stale handling are mandatory, but the core does not define cancellation triggers, which requests are cancellable, post-timeout UI state, error presentation, or late-response correlation beyond the stale-discard constraint.
items.impact: Equivalent clients can show inconsistent loading, cancellation, and failure behavior and can disagree on when a response is stale.
items.builder_discretion: Define request identity, cancel triggers, terminal states, and user-visible timeout behavior.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Hover, completion, documentSymbol, definition, references, breadcrumbs, and go-to-symbol features use LSP when available, enforce timeout/cancel/stale handling, and accept completion when hover, completion, breadcrumbs, symbol, and definition navigation work correctly.

items.title: FileSafe authority for LSP workspace edits
items.statement: Code actions and workspace edits must pass through FileSafe-backed workspace/applyEdit rather than bypassing the file-safety authority.

evidence.exact_quote: - Code actions and workspace edits must route through FileSafe-backed workspace/applyEdit.

items.title: Workspace-edit rejection and partial-failure behavior are unspecified
items.statement: The routing authority is explicit, but no outcome contract is given for FileSafe denial, malformed edits, overlapping edits, partial multi-file application, rollback, user notification, or the response returned to the server.
items.impact: A multi-file code action can leave ambiguous disk state and ambiguous protocol acknowledgement after a failed edit.
items.builder_discretion: Choose validation, atomicity, rollback, acknowledgement, and error-UI semantics.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Inlay hints, semantic tokens, signature help, code actions, and code lens render or invoke through editor affordances, with code actions and workspace edits routed through FileSafe-backed workspace/applyEdit.

items.title: Status, disable, and heuristic fallback transitions
items.statement: The status bar shows server state, disabling a server stops LSP, and absence or disablement of LSP selects a heuristic outline without presenting fallback as healthy LSP.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Status and fallback behavior show LSP state in the status bar, honor per-server enable/disable, use heuristic fallback when no server is available, and may show optional install hints without claiming healthy LSP capability.
- Fallback heuristic behavior must not masquerade as healthy LSP state.

items.title: Status vocabulary and degraded-state mapping are undefined
items.statement: The UI must show server state but the core does not enumerate states or map spawning, initializing, ready, disabled, timed out, crashed, restarting, and fallback conditions to status text and affordances.
items.impact: The status bar can communicate materially different health truth across implementations.
items.builder_discretion: Choose the state model, display labels, transitions, and whether install hints appear in each state.

evidence.exact_quote: - Status bar shows server state

items.title: Assistant and Interview consume current diagnostics
items.statement: When context is composed, Assistant and Interview receive current diagnostic lists for relevant files.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Current diagnostics are included in Assistant and Interview context so agents receive diagnostic lists for relevant files when composing context.

items.title: Diagnostic context privacy and selection boundaries are absent
items.statement: Diagnostics are propagated to agent context, but the core does not define consent, redaction, trust-boundary checks, maximum payload, severity filtering, deduplication, or the algorithm that determines relevant files.
items.impact: Diagnostic text and paths can expose sensitive project content or unpredictably consume context budget.
items.builder_discretion: Choose relevance, filtering, redaction, consent, and payload-budget rules.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Current diagnostics are included in Assistant and Interview context so agents receive diagnostic lists for relevant files when composing context.

items.title: Configuration locations, precedence, and merge contract
items.statement: App configuration lives under config.lsp, project overrides live at .puppet-master/lsp.json, app values are applied before project values, arrays replace, absent keys inherit, and server-specific settings resolve by server id before language or filetype mapping.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: MVP LSP config closes implementation policy by storing app-level config under config.lsp, project overrides at .puppet-master/lsp.json, applying app then project precedence, replacing arrays, inheriting absent keys, and resolving server-specific settings by server id before language/filetype mapping.

items.title: Invalid configuration and migration behavior are unspecified
items.statement: The merge contract does not define schema/version handling, malformed JSON behavior, type conflicts, unknown keys, invalid server references, user-visible errors, fallback to last-known-good configuration, or migration between config shapes; compatibility notes are explicitly empty.
items.impact: A bad project override can produce divergent startup, silent fallback, or loss of valid app-level settings.
items.builder_discretion: Choose validation, error recovery, unknown-key policy, and migration/version semantics.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: MVP LSP config closes implementation policy by storing app-level config under config.lsp, project overrides at .puppet-master/lsp.json, applying app then project precedence, replacing arrays, inheriting absent keys, and resolving server-specific settings by server id before language/filetype mapping.

items.title: LSP owner boundary is explicit
items.statement: Plans/LSPSupport.md owns LSP-specific protocol and client constraints while referenced owner documents retain their SSOT boundaries.

items.title: Runtime acceptance oracles are not bound to validation surfaces
items.statement: The units state user-visible and runtime acceptance behavior, but their declared validation surfaces only validate plan migration and indexing; no executable oracle is specified for protocol lifecycle, diagnostics, editor interactions, fallback truth, context propagation, or config merging.
items.impact: Governance checks can pass without demonstrating that any required LSP behavior works.
items.builder_discretion: Choose runtime test fixtures, protocol fakes, UI interaction checks, and pass/fail assertions.

items.title: Planning units forbid premature executable task creation
items.statement: The reviewed units explicitly prevent creation of WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, and production build tasks in this planning phase.

evidence.exact_quote: - No WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, or production build tasks are created.

items.title: Performance and resource bounds are absent from the core
items.statement: The core requires debounced changes and multiple interactive LSP features but does not bind debounce duration, concurrency, queueing, cache limits, diagnostic volume, registry capacity, process count, or latency budgets.
items.impact: Implementations can satisfy functional prose while becoming unresponsive or resource-heavy on large workspaces.
items.builder_discretion: Choose concurrency, debounce, timeout, cache, payload, and process-resource limits.

- timeout and cancel

items.title: Required implementation ordering is not represented
items.statement: Every reviewed feature unit declares no dependencies even though diagnostics, navigation, semantic features, status, and diagnostic context consume the client, lifecycle, registry, transport, and sync foundation described by LSPS-062.
items.impact: A compiler or builder can schedule dependent feature work without the prerequisite lifecycle and synchronization substrate.
items.builder_discretion: Infer dependency ordering between the foundation and each consuming feature.

dimension_assessments.summary: The core states lifecycle, sync, diagnostics, editor-feature, fallback, context, and configuration behaviors.
Required LSP foundation and editor capabilities are enumerated.
Inputs and outputs include document events, diagnostics per URI, LSP requests and responses, workspace edits, configuration, UI presentation, and agent context.
FileSafe and config merge contracts are explicit, but request cancellation and edit failure outcomes remain incomplete.
Enable, disable, fallback, and stale rejection are stated; lifecycle recovery and diagnostic freshness transitions are missing.
The LSP document boundary and FileSafe edit authority are explicit.
LSPSupport ownership is named, but concrete cross-owner contracts for UI, FileSafe, Assistant, and Interview are not bound.
UI, Problems, gutter, status bar, editor features, Assistant, and Interview consumers are identified.
Required visible outcomes are stated, but the exact status vocabulary and degraded-state mapping are not.
Lifecycle, workspace-edit, diagnostic, and request failure recovery is under-specified.
FileSafe protects workspace edits, but diagnostic propagation lacks privacy and trust-boundary rules.
Diagnostics and edits have downstream routes, but PlanUnit dependency propagation is absent.
Server lifecycle is required without operational recovery or runtime observability and validation behavior.
Interactive and debounced behavior lacks bounded concurrency, latency, payload, cache, and process limits.
Config precedence is defined, while versioning, invalid-input fallback, and migration are not; compatibility notes are empty.
Behavioral outcomes are prose-level; declared validators cover plan artifacts rather than executable LSP behavior.
Consequential discretion remains for recovery, request state, edit atomicity, status truth, privacy, config errors, runtime tests, scale, and dependency ordering.
The reviewed core leaves multiple consequential policies unstated; these are recorded as bounded gaps without inferring behavior from outside the window.
